Marrow Wrack.narrative: I came down the fish road from Kettlebridge after the Surge with my wife and daughter and what tools I could carry. I build in concrete and salvage because that's what the quay has, but I know stone, and the seawall should be stone from the ridge, not the overpriced stuff Crane sends. Gideon Fenwick took my work and slandered me, and I won't set foot in Kettlebridge while he has a yard there. I owe Josiah Crane for a load of brick, and that debt sits on me like a wet coat.
goals: build the seawall in stone from the ridge
clear my debt to Josiah Crane
see Gideon Fenwick get his due
keep my family fed and housed
learn to read the tide tables well enough to plan a season's work ahead
make something with his hands that Nia will keep after him — a good table, a strong door

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She's the only one who knows what we lost in Kettlebridge, and she still stands by me.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's got her mother's sense and my stubbornness; I want better for her than a borrowed boat.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: We patch the lower quay together and curse the stone price together.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He holds my brick debt and I can't pay it yet.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: He took my work and slandered me; I won't forget.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She wants the seawall as much as I do, and she listens when I talk stone.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She and Odile work together; a good woman with a bone-setting hand.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Odile trades herbs with her; she keeps a good room of salves.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: Another man who came down the road and found the door shut; we drink to it when he's down.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: quay neighbour
relations.note: She cooks a good fried fish and pays on time, but she took Fenwick's word over mine when the tale came down the fish road — I'll build her stone stall when there's stone to be had, and watch her while I do it.

memories.gist: The quarrel with Gideon Fenwick over the job and the brick load; he said I cheated him, and the whole yard heard.
Packing our things and walking down the fish road after the Surge, with Odile and Nia and a handcart of tools.
The first time I saw the lower quay after the surge: broken concrete, salt-eaten timber, and no stone anywhere.
Setting the first salvage beam on the lower quay with Ostrander Vane, and him saying we'd build it proper one day.
Borrowing the load of brick from Josiah Crane on a handshake and a promise, and the look he gave me.

stances.why: Concrete and salvage won't hold against the next surge; the ridge has good stone.
Fenwick's yard is there, and I won't give him the satisfaction.
I owe Crane for the brick, and I'll pay it even if it takes a year.
Odile and Nia are all I have left from the old life.
They sell stone dear and call it fair trade.

Marrow Wrack.secret: I once took a small block of dressed stone from a Kettlebridge yard without paying, the week before we left. I tell myself it was owed wages.
pastimes: walking the shore at low tide, turning over stone and salvage to see what the sea's given back
sitting on the unfinished seawall with a mug of something hot, watching the boats come in
mending his own tools and boots by the lamp, slowly and well
Marrow Wrack.calling: I build to last — concrete and salvage where I must, but stone is what a wall wants, and I know stone.

Odile Wrack.narrative: I keep a healer's room behind the fish market and set the builders' bones when they fall. I came down from Kettlebridge with Marrow and Nia after the Surge, and the cold welcome we got there still stings. I know the quarrel cost us our house, and I wish Marrow would let it go, but I won't say so to his face. I want Nia settled with a man who has a roof, not a man who borrows boats.
goals: keep my family healthy and fed
see Nia married to someone steady
build up my stock of salves
grow her stock of salves until she can sell a little beyond the quay
see Nia settled with a man who has a roof of his own

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man with a hard head; I wish he'd let the Fenwick quarrel lie.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's got a good heart, but she doesn't see what debts can do to a household.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: We set bones together and share what herbs we can.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: She knows her herbs, and she worries about the winter cough like I do.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: herb trader
relations.note: She's a strange one, but her salves are good.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A cheerful lad, but he owes half the quay and borrows boats.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She keeps Nia in work at her noodle stall.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She's a good woman, but her son needs to stand on his own.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: His quarrel took our house and our town from us; I will not forget it, whatever Marrow says.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He patches the lower quay with salvage and wants proper stone; he took Marrow's side against Fenwick, and I remember that.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She cooks at the fish market and wants her stall in stone; a hard worker, and she does not carry tales about my daughter.

memories.gist: The morning we left Kettlebridge: the neighbours looking away, and the cold rain on the fish road.
Setting a quarryman's leg in Kettlebridge before the Surge, and him swearing I had the gentlest hands on the ridge.
Nia's first day at Ilse Ostrander's stall, and how proud she looked with her own apron.
Marrow coming home with the brick load and the debt to Crane, and me knowing we'd be paying for it for months.
The first winter on the quay, when the cough took half the poor terrace and Mira and I ran out of salve.

stances.why: A man who borrows boats will borrow bread, and I won't have Nia go hungry.
I set bones for anyone who comes, Kettlebridge or quay, because that's what a healer does.
The quarrel cost us our house, and I wish Marrow would let it go, though I won't say so to him.
They turned their backs on us when we needed work, and I don't forget.
The winter cough takes the poor terrace every year, and I mean to have salve and fuel.

Odile Wrack.secret: I wrote to my sister in Kettlebridge last month, without telling Marrow, to ask if there was work for him there if the quarrel could be mended.
pastimes: gathering herbs and seaweed along the rocks at dawn for her salves
sitting with Maren Vane over tea, trading gossip and complaints about their men
listening to the singers at the inn on a slow night, though she never sings herself
Odile Wrack.calling: I set bones and mend what's broken — a healer's hands are the work I'd choose again.

Nia Wrack.narrative: I cook at Ilse Ostrander's noodle stall and I want a stall of my own one day. Jory Pike makes me laugh and he knows boats better than anyone, but my mother measures him by his debts and I can't blame her. I like Tam Harrow too, but Jory's the one who makes me feel like the quay is a place I could belong. I wish my father would let the Kettlebridge quarrel go, but I'd never say so.
goals: save enough for my own stall
see where things go with Jory Pike
keep my parents from worrying too much
save enough marks for her own stall and a good pot of her own
learn Ilse's noodle recipes properly, every one of them

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: father
relations.note: He's stubborn as stone, but he'd do anything for me.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She wants me settled, and she's probably right, but she doesn't see how Jory makes me laugh.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She's taught me most of what I know about a noodle pot.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He's cheerful and he knows boats, and he makes me feel like the quay is home.

relations.name: Tam Harrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He's a good lad, but he's not Jory.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We work the stalls together and she knows everyone's business.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Jory's mother is kind, but she worries about him like I do.

relations.name: Rook Fenner the younger
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Tam's cousin; a quiet lad with quick hands for a knot.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She sets bones and trades gossip with my mother; a kind woman with a sharp eye.

memories.gist: The first time I cooked a whole pot of noodles at Ilse's stall without burning them, and she nodded once.
Jory Pike bringing me a handful of harbour flowers and not knowing where to look.
My mother setting a fisherman's arm in our room while I held the lamp and tried not to look.
The night the tide lanterns were lit late and a boat came in wrong; my father cursing the wardens.
Walking the fish road with my father when I was small, before the Surge, and him showing me the ridge stone.

stances.why: I won't cook at someone else's fire forever.
He makes me laugh and he's kind, and debts can be paid.
My parents came down the road for me, and I won't shame them.
I won't say what I think about the Kettlebridge quarrel; it only makes my father angry.
A hot bowl on a cold night is worth more than a mark in the box.

Nia Wrack.secret: I've been putting aside a few marks each week for a stall of my own, and I haven't told my mother, because she'd want it for the winter store.
pastimes: cooking for the stall and trying new broths on Sella Mackerel for honest opinions
walking the harbour at night to look at the tide lanterns
laughing with Jory Pike on the boats, learning the names of rigging and wind
Nia Wrack.calling: I cook at Ilse's stall, and one day the stall will be mine, with my name on it.
